questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: MDR-TB is defined as resistance to:

options.label: A
options.explanation: MDR-TB means resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin, the two most potent first-line drugs.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rifampicin resistance (rpoB mutation, detected by GeneXpert) is one of the two defining resistances of MDR-TB.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ethambutol resistance may coexist but is not part of the definition; MDR needs only INH plus rifampicin resistance.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pyrazinamide resistance is not required for MDR-TB; M. bovis is naturally pyrazinamide resistant.

questions.pearl: XDR-TB = MDR plus resistance to a fluoroquinolone and at least one other group A drug (bedaquiline or linezolid) under the 2021 WHO definition.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Factors involved in regulation of arterial blood pressure:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Mean arterial pressure = cardiac output x total peripheral resistance, so CO is a direct determinant.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Peripheral vascular resistance is the same as systemic vascular resistance and is the other main determinant of MAP, mostly set by arterioles.

options.label: C
options.explanation: SVR, set chiefly by arteriolar tone, multiplies with cardiac output to give MAP.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Strictly, MAP - CVP = CO x SVR; CVP also governs venous return and hence preload and cardiac output.

questions.pearl: MAP = DBP + 1/3 pulse pressure; arterioles are the main resistance vessels and the site of short-term BP control.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: The wet (ascitic) type is the commonest form, with exudative, lymphocyte-rich fluid and high SAAG-negative protein.

options.label: B
options.explanation: TB peritonitis causes weight loss, fever and night sweats from chronic infection; abdominal girth may rise but body weight falls.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Vague abdominal pain and distension are among the commonest presenting complaints.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A thickened, rolled omentum is a finding of the fibrous type rather than a general clinical feature; the classic picture is ascites with a doughy abdomen.

questions.pearl: Ascitic ADA above 39 U/L strongly supports TB peritonitis; laparoscopy with peritoneal biopsy is the definitive test.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Minimum monitoring for a patient in shock:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bailey & Love lists ECG, pulse oximetry, blood pressure and urine output as the minimum monitoring in shock.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hourly urine output via a catheter is a key minimum measure of end-organ perfusion (target over 0.5 mL/kg/h).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cardiac output measurement is part of extended (invasive) monitoring, not the minimum set.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Base deficit and lactate belong to extended monitoring, used to judge occult hypoperfusion and resuscitation end points.

questions.pearl: Minimum shock monitoring: ECG, pulse oximetry, BP, urine output. Extended: CVP, invasive BP, cardiac output, base deficit, lactate.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Indications of laparoscopy as a diagnostic tool in gynaecology:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Laparoscopy allows direct visualisation and characterisation of adnexal masses, and often treatment at the same sitting.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cervical cancer is detected by Pap smear, VIA, colposcopy and biopsy; the cervix is not seen at laparoscopy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Laparoscopy with biopsy is the gold standard for diagnosing and staging endometriosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Intrauterine lesions such as polyps are diagnosed and removed by hysteroscopy, not laparoscopy.

questions.pearl: Laparoscopy is the gold standard for endometriosis, ectopic pregnancy diagnosis and tubal patency (chromopertubation).

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.text: Organs revert back to pre-pregnant state
options.explanation: The puerperium is the ~6 weeks after delivery during which the genital organs return to the non-pregnant state.

options.label: B
options.text: There may be retention of urine
options.explanation: Bladder oedema, reduced sensitivity and perineal pain commonly cause urinary retention in the first days.

options.label: C
options.text: Involution rate of uterus about 1.5 cm/day
options.explanation: The fundus descends roughly 1-1.5 cm a day and is no longer palpable abdominally by about day 10-14.

options.label: D
options.text: Lochia rubra present in first 10 days
options.explanation: Lochia rubra lasts only 1-4 days; it is followed by lochia serosa (5-9 days) and alba (10-15 days).

questions.pearl: Uterus weighs ~1 kg after delivery, ~500 g at 1 week and ~60 g by 6 weeks.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bacterial meningitis produces a polymorphonuclear pleocytosis, often over 1000 cells/uL.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bacteria and neutrophils consume glucose; CSF:blood glucose ratio usually falls below 0.4.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Breakdown of the blood-brain barrier raises CSF protein, often above 1 g/L.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acid-fast bacilli indicate tuberculous meningitis, which shows lymphocytes, very high protein and low glucose.

questions.pearl: Turbid CSF, neutrophils, low glucose, high protein = bacterial; lymphocytes, normal glucose = viral; cobweb clot with AFB = TB.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.text: Makes up to 5% of body weight in the neonate
options.explanation: Brown fat forms about 2-6% of neonatal body weight and is the main source of non-shivering thermogenesis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: It lies mainly between the scapulae, around the neck, mediastinum, kidneys and adrenals, not in the abdominal wall.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Brown fat regresses after infancy; adults retain only small depots in the neck and supraclavicular areas.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Active brown fat burns glucose and fatty acids and improves, rather than decreases, insulin sensitivity.

questions.pearl: Brown fat heat comes from uncoupling protein 1 (thermogenin) in its abundant mitochondria, driven by sympathetic noradrenaline.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Indications of vitamin A supplementation (according to IMCI):

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dysentery is treated with antibiotics (ciprofloxacin) and zinc; it is not an IMCI trigger for vitamin A.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Persistent diarrhoea is an IMCI indication for a therapeutic dose of vitamin A.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Vitamin A in measles cuts mortality and prevents corneal complications; two doses are given on consecutive days.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Severe acute malnutrition is an indication because body stores of vitamin A are depleted.

questions.pearl: Vitamin A dose: 50,000 IU under 6 months, 100,000 IU at 6-11 months, 200,000 IU from 12 months.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Basal ganglia disease causes rigidity (increased tone); hypotonia is a cerebellar or lower motor neurone sign.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A pill-rolling tremor at rest, improving with movement, is typical of nigrostriatal dysfunction.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Parkinsonism (bradykinesia, rigidity, tremor) is the classic basal ganglia syndrome from dopamine loss.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Scanning (staccato) speech is a cerebellar sign; parkinsonian speech is hypophonic and monotonous.

questions.pearl: Cerebellar signs mnemonic DANISH: dysdiadochokinesia, ataxia, nystagmus, intention tremor, scanning speech, hypotonia.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Oral budesonide induces remission in mild to moderate ileocaecal Crohn's with little systemic steroid effect.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sulfasalazine has a modest role in mild colonic Crohn's disease, being more effective in ulcerative colitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Azathioprine is a thiopurine used to maintain remission and spare steroids.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lactose is not a treatment; lactose intolerance may coexist and some patients are advised to avoid it.

questions.pearl: Smoking cessation is the single most effective measure to reduce Crohn's relapse.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Heart failure causes ADH and renin activation with water retention exceeding sodium, diluting plasma sodium.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Low effective circulating volume drives ADH release and water retention in an oedematous patient.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Diarrhoea causes depletional (hypovolaemic) hyponatraemia from loss of sodium-containing fluid.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Diuretics, especially thiazides, cause depletional hyponatraemia through urinary sodium loss.

questions.pearl: Dilutional (hypervolaemic) hyponatraemia: CCF, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome, renal failure; SIADH is euvolaemic.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Glycosuria causes osmotic diuresis in diabetes mellitus, and ADH lack or resistance causes water diuresis in diabetes insipidus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Diuretics block tubular sodium reabsorption, causing natriuresis and diuresis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Nephrotic syndrome causes sodium and water retention with oedema, not increased urine output.

options.label: D
options.explanation: SIADH means excess ADH, causing antidiuresis with concentrated urine and dilutional hyponatraemia.

questions.pearl: Polyuria is urine output over 3 L/day; check serum glucose, calcium and urine osmolality first.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bowing of the legs is a feature of rickets (vitamin D deficiency), not scurvy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Infants with scurvy are irritable and cry when handled because of painful subperiosteal haemorrhages.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pain from subperiosteal bleeding makes the infant keep the legs still in a frog position (pseudoparalysis).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Craniotabes (softening of skull bones) is a sign of rickets.

questions.pearl: Scurvy: bleeding gums, perifollicular haemorrhages, corkscrew hairs, scorbutic rosary (sharp) versus rachitic rosary (rounded).

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Immediate management after a baby is born:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Immediate drying and warming prevents hypothermia and stimulates breathing (essential newborn care).

options.label: B
options.text: Clamping and cutting the umbilical cord
options.explanation: The cord is clamped and cut with a clean instrument, ideally after 1-3 minutes (delayed clamping).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Vitamin K 1 mg IM at birth prevents haemorrhagic disease of the newborn.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Birth vaccines (BCG, OPV-0, hepatitis B) are given before discharge, not as part of immediate care at delivery.

questions.pearl: Essential newborn care: dry, warm, skin-to-skin, delayed cord clamping, breastfeeding within 1 hour, vitamin K, eye care.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Keloids show a familial tendency, often autosomal dominant with variable penetrance.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Presternal area, shoulders, earlobes and upper back are classic sites.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Keloids persist and keep growing beyond the wound margin; hypertrophic scars regress with time.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Keloids are much more common in dark-skinned (black) people.

questions.pearl: Keloid extends beyond the scar and recurs after excision; hypertrophic scar stays within it and regresses.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Marrow infiltration by leukaemic cells reduces megakaryocyte production of platelets.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Alcohol suppresses the marrow directly, and associated hypersplenism and folate deficiency add to it.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Immune thrombocytopenia destroys antibody-coated platelets in the spleen.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Platelets are consumed in widespread microthrombi in disseminated intravascular coagulation.

questions.pearl: Always exclude pseudothrombocytopenia (EDTA-induced clumping) by checking a citrate sample or the film.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Physiological jaundice appears after 24 hours, usually on day 2-3; jaundice in the first 24 hours is pathological.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Signs of sepsis suggest pathological jaundice; physiological jaundice occurs in a well baby.

options.label: C
options.text: Duration of jaundice less than 7 days
options.explanation: In term babies it usually lasts 7-10 days and may last up to 14 days, longer in preterms.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bilirubin rises slowly, under 5 mg/dL per day; a faster rise is pathological.

questions.pearl: Pathological jaundice: within 24 h, rise over 5 mg/dL/day, conjugated over 2 mg/dL, or lasting beyond 2 weeks in a term baby.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hypertensive retinopathy (AV nipping, haemorrhages, papilloedema) is a target-organ complication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: LV hypertrophy and atrial dilatation from hypertension predispose to AF.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Nephrosclerosis from sustained hypertension causes chronic kidney disease.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Chronic glomerulonephritis is a cause of secondary hypertension, not its complication.

questions.pearl: Renal parenchymal disease is the commonest cause of secondary hypertension.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Uncontrolled bleeding from a shattered splenic injury is the commonest indication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Splenectomy stops destruction of spherocytes and corrects the anaemia, ideally after age 6.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Aplastic anaemia is marrow failure; splenectomy does not help and treatment is immunosuppression or transplant.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Kala-azar is treated with antileishmanial drugs (liposomal amphotericin B, miltefosine); the spleen regresses with therapy.

questions.pearl: Give pneumococcal, Hib and meningococcal vaccines at least 2 weeks before elective splenectomy.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fexofenadine is a second-generation H1 antihistamine used for allergies.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ranitidine is an H2 blocker that reduces gastric acid secretion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loratadine is a non-sedating H1 antihistamine.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Famotidine is the most potent H2 blocker with no antiandrogenic or enzyme-inhibiting effect.

questions.pearl: Cimetidine inhibits cytochrome P450 and has antiandrogenic effects (gynaecomastia); famotidine does not.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Treponema pallidum crosses the placenta, especially after 16 weeks, causing congenital syphilis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: HIV can pass transplacentally, though most transmission occurs during delivery and breastfeeding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Measles in pregnancy causes abortion or preterm birth, but transplacental congenital infection is rare.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rubella crosses the placenta and causes congenital rubella syndrome, worst in the first trimester.

questions.pearl: TORCH: toxoplasma, others (syphilis, varicella, parvovirus B19, HIV), rubella, CMV, herpes.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Microvascular damage causes diabetic retinopathy, a leading cause of blindness in adults.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Peripheral sensory neuropathy in a glove-and-stocking pattern is the commonest complication.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Macrovascular atherosclerosis increases the risk of stroke two- to four-fold.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Neuropathy plus ischaemia leads to diabetic foot ulcers.

questions.pearl: Microvascular: retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy. Macrovascular: coronary, cerebral and peripheral arterial disease.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Bacteria that can penetrate intact corneal epithelium:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Neisseria gonorrhoeae can invade intact corneal epithelium and perforate the cornea rapidly.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is a common cause of keratitis but needs an epithelial breach.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Haemophilus (aegyptius) is classically listed among organisms that penetrate intact epithelium.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Corynebacterium diphtheriae is one of the organisms that can invade the normal cornea.

questions.pearl: Intact cornea invaders: N. gonorrhoeae, N. meningitidis, C. diphtheriae, H. aegyptius, Listeria.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: RA causes exudative pleural effusions with characteristically very low glucose.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mononeuritis multiplex from vasculitis and entrapment neuropathy (carpal tunnel) occur.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Kidney involvement is uncommon and usually secondary to amyloidosis or drugs, not a direct feature.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hepatitis is not an extra-articular feature of RA; liver injury is usually drug-related (methotrexate).

questions.pearl: Felty's syndrome: RA, splenomegaly and neutropenia.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Muscles supplied by the axillary nerve:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Teres major is supplied by the lower subscapular nerve.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The axillary nerve (C5, C6) supplies deltoid, so injury causes loss of shoulder abduction beyond 15 degrees.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Triceps is supplied by the radial nerve, not the axillary nerve.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The axillary nerve supplies teres minor, its posterior branch giving a nerve to it.

questions.pearl: Axillary nerve injury (surgical neck fracture, shoulder dislocation): deltoid paralysis and regimental badge sensory loss.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Free T3 is measured, particularly to detect T3 thyrotoxicosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Free T4 is a core thyroid function test along with TSH.

options.label: C
options.explanation: TSH is the most sensitive first-line test for primary thyroid disease.

options.label: D
options.explanation: TRH is a hypothalamic hormone not measured routinely; the TRH stimulation test is obsolete.

questions.pearl: Low TSH with normal FT4 and FT3 = subclinical hyperthyroidism; raised TSH with normal FT4 = subclinical hypothyroidism.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Olanzapine is an atypical antipsychotic (D2/5-HT2A blocker) with marked weight gain.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fluoxetine is an SSRI antidepressant.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Quetiapine is an atypical antipsychotic also used in bipolar depression.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sertraline is an SSRI antidepressant.

questions.pearl: Clozapine is reserved for treatment-resistant schizophrenia because of agranulocytosis; monitor the blood count.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Urine hCG tests turn positive around the time of the missed period.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Serum progesterone assesses viability or ectopic risk but does not diagnose pregnancy; serum beta-hCG does.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Transvaginal USG shows a gestational sac at about 4.5-5 weeks and confirms intrauterine pregnancy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: X-ray is avoided because of radiation and shows fetal skeleton only after 16 weeks.

questions.pearl: A gestational sac should be seen on TVS when serum beta-hCG exceeds about 1500-2000 IU/L (discriminatory zone).

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: History and examination form the first part of triple assessment.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Imaging (mammography over 35 years, ultrasound in younger women) is the second part.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Tissue diagnosis by FNAC or preferably core-needle biopsy is the third part.

options.label: D
options.explanation: CT is used for staging metastatic disease, not for triple assessment.

questions.pearl: Triple assessment = clinical + imaging + pathology; all three concordant gives over 99% diagnostic accuracy.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: High-risk HPV 16 and 18 cause cervical, anal and oropharyngeal cancers via E6 (p53) and E7 (Rb) proteins.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chronic HBV infection causes hepatocellular carcinoma, partly through viral DNA integration.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HIV is not directly oncogenic; AIDS-related cancers arise from immunosuppression and co-infection with KSHV or EBV.

options.label: D
options.explanation: EBV is linked to Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma and Hodgkin lymphoma.

questions.pearl: HTLV-1 causes adult T-cell leukaemia; HHV-8 causes Kaposi sarcoma; HCV causes HCC without DNA integration.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Higher temperature outside the scrotum damages spermatogenesis, especially if bilateral and uncorrected.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A patent processus vaginalis accompanies most undescended testes, causing indirect hernia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Risk of germ cell tumour (mostly seminoma) is several times higher, even after orchidopexy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hydrocele is not a recognised complication; torsion and trauma are the other classic ones.

questions.pearl: Orchidopexy is recommended at 6-12 months of age, and completed by 18 months.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cold causes peripheral vasoconstriction and slow flow, producing peripheral cyanosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cyanosis needs about 5 g/dL of deoxygenated haemoglobin, rarely reached when total haemoglobin is very low.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pulmonary oedema impairs gas exchange, causing central cyanosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Right-to-left shunting across the VSD causes central cyanosis; it is the commonest cyanotic congenital heart disease.

questions.pearl: Cyanosis appears early in polycythaemia and late or never in severe anaemia.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Affected individuals are homozygous; heterozygotes are clinically normal carriers.

options.label: B
options.explanation: When both parents are carriers, 25% of offspring are affected.

options.label: C
options.explanation: With two carrier parents, 50% of children are heterozygous carriers.

options.label: D
options.text: Males are more affected than females
options.explanation: Both sexes are affected equally; male predominance suggests X-linked inheritance.

questions.pearl: Carrier x carrier: 25% affected, 50% carriers, 25% normal. Consanguinity raises AR disease risk.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Raised metabolic rate and thermogenesis cause heat intolerance and sweating.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Increased cardiac output causes systolic hypertension with a wide pulse pressure.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Thyrotoxicosis causes oligomenorrhoea or amenorrhoea; menorrhagia is a feature of hypothyroidism.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Increased gut motility causes frequent stools or diarrhoea; constipation suggests hypothyroidism.

questions.pearl: In the elderly, thyrotoxicosis may present only with AF, weight loss or apathy (apathetic thyrotoxicosis).

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Babies are hypotonic and sluggish, with a large protruding tongue and umbilical hernia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Untreated hypothyroidism causes growth failure with delayed bone age.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Constipation, not diarrhoea, is typical.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Delayed skull ossification leaves large anterior and posterior fontanelles.

questions.pearl: Neonatal TSH screening is vital; starting levothyroxine within 2 weeks preserves normal IQ.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chalazion is a chronic lipogranulomatous inflammation of a blocked meibomian gland.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Acute suppurative infection of the gland of Zeis is a stye (external hordeolum).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Moll glands are modified sweat glands; their infection also causes a stye or cyst of Moll.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Krause glands are accessory lacrimal glands in the conjunctival fornix, unrelated to chalazion.

questions.pearl: A recurrent chalazion in an older adult needs biopsy to exclude meibomian (sebaceous) gland carcinoma.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cystic hygroma is a brilliantly transilluminant lymphatic malformation in the posterior triangle.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Thyroglossal cyst is a midline swelling that moves upwards on protruding the tongue.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Lymph nodes along the jugular chain are the commonest lateral neck swelling.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ranula is a mucous retention cyst in the floor of the mouth; only a plunging ranula extends into the neck.

questions.pearl: Midline neck swellings: thyroglossal cyst, thyroid isthmus, dermoid, sublingual dermoid, submental nodes.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Adenoids block the Eustachian tube opening and seed infection, causing recurrent acute otitis media.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Persistent tubal dysfunction and infection predispose to chronic suppurative otitis media.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Nasal obstruction produces hyponasal speech (rhinolalia clausa).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Subglottic stenosis follows prolonged intubation or congenital narrowing, not adenoid hypertrophy.

questions.pearl: Adenoid facies: open mouth, pinched nose, high-arched palate, crowded teeth and a dull expression.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: High vaginal swab culture detects infection, not malignancy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Speculum examination, VIA and colposcopy identify suspicious lesions for biopsy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Punch or cone biopsy gives the histological diagnosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hysteroscopy assesses the endometrial cavity; it is not used to diagnose cervical cancer.

questions.pearl: Cervical cancer is staged clinically (FIGO), now supplemented by imaging and pathology.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hepatitis A spreads faeco-orally; blood transmission is very rare because viraemia is brief.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hepatitis B is highly infectious via blood, sex and perinatally.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HIV spreads through blood, sexual contact and vertically.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hepatitis C is mainly blood-borne, e.g. injecting drug use and unsafe transfusions.

questions.pearl: Needle-stick risk rule of 3s: HBV about 30%, HCV about 3%, HIV about 0.3%.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Vomiting and diarrhoea cause hypovolaemic hyponatraemia, worsened by hypotonic replacement.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Heavy sweating and burns lose sodium, causing hypovolaemic hyponatraemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hypothyroidism reduces free water excretion through ADH and lower GFR, causing euvolaemic hyponatraemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Water intake beyond renal excretory capacity (over ~15 L/day) causes dilutional hyponatraemia with dilute urine.

questions.pearl: Correct chronic hyponatraemia by no more than 8-10 mmol/L in 24 hours to avoid osmotic demyelination.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Campylobacter invades colonic mucosa and commonly causes bloody diarrhoea.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Typhoid usually causes fever with constipation or pea-soup diarrhoea; bleeding occurs only with ulcer complications.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Shigella is the classic cause of bacillary dysentery with blood and mucus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Eggs in the colonic wall cause intestinal schistosomiasis with bloody diarrhoea.

questions.pearl: Bloody diarrhoea: Shigella, Campylobacter, EHEC, Salmonella, Entamoeba histolytica, plus IBD.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Disseminated tuberculosis can cause generalised lymphadenopathy, though cervical nodes are most typical.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Generalised, non-tender lymphadenopathy is common in active lupus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: CMV causes an infectious mononucleosis-like illness with generalised lymphadenopathy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lymph node enlargement in measles is mild and not a characteristic feature; rubella is the classic exanthem with marked lymphadenopathy.

questions.pearl: Generalised lymphadenopathy: infections (EBV, CMV, HIV, TB), lymphoma, leukaemia, SLE, sarcoidosis, drugs (phenytoin).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ampicillin is an extended-spectrum penicillin acting on gram-positive and many gram-negative organisms.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Streptomycin is a narrow-spectrum aminoglycoside acting mainly on aerobic gram-negative bacilli and mycobacteria.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Amoxicillin has the same broad spectrum as ampicillin with better oral absorption.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Chloramphenicol is a classic broad-spectrum antibiotic covering gram-positives, gram-negatives, anaerobes and rickettsiae.

questions.pearl: Classic broad-spectrum agents: tetracyclines and chloramphenicol; chloramphenicol in neonates causes grey baby syndrome.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Clinical features of acute viral hepatitis:

options.label: A
options.explanation: A prodrome of low-grade fever, anorexia and nausea precedes jaundice.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hepatocellular injury causes jaundice with dark urine in the icteric phase.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Malaise and fatigue are prominent prodromal symptoms.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Varices result from portal hypertension in chronic liver disease, not acute hepatitis.

questions.pearl: Aminotransferases often exceed 1000 IU/L in acute viral hepatitis, ALT higher than AST.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Inflammation of the gallbladder causes fever and tachycardia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Constant right upper quadrant pain with a positive Murphy's sign is the hallmark.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mild jaundice occurs in a minority from oedema, Mirizzi syndrome or coexisting duct stones.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Mucocele follows stone impaction in a non-infected gallbladder; it is a complication, not a feature of acute cholecystitis.

questions.pearl: Ultrasound is the first-line imaging: thick wall, pericholecystic fluid and sonographic Murphy's sign.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Topical steroid therapy in eye disease is avoided in:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Steroids can cause posterior subcapsular cataract, but cataract is not a contraindication; steroids are routinely used after cataract surgery.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Steroids worsen infective (especially herpetic and fungal) corneal ulcers and risk perforation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Steroids raise intraocular pressure (steroid responders), so they are avoided in glaucoma.

options.label: D
options.explanation: After foreign body removal the epithelial defect can become infected; steroids delay healing and favour infection.

questions.pearl: Never give topical steroids for an undiagnosed red eye: dendritic ulcer can progress to geographic ulcer.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Biochemical changes in gastric outlet obstruction:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Loss of gastric juice with dehydration usually causes hyponatraemia, not hypernatraemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Potassium is lost in vomitus and urine, giving hypokalaemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loss of HCl causes hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The kidney retains Na+ and K+ in exchange for H+, producing acid urine despite alkalosis.

questions.pearl: Resuscitate GOO with 0.9% saline plus potassium; it corrects the alkalosis by restoring chloride.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Giardia lamblia lives in the duodenum and jejunum, causing malabsorption and steatorrhoea.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Adult Ascaris lumbricoides lives in the small intestine and may cause obstruction.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Schistosoma mansoni and japonicum inhabit mesenteric veins and cause intestinal disease.

options.label: D
options.explanation: In humans Echinococcus forms hydatid cysts in the liver and lungs; the adult worm lives in the dog intestine.

questions.pearl: Humans are the intermediate host for Echinococcus granulosus; the dog is the definitive host.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Specific gravity reflects concentrating ability and is part of physical examination of urine.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Colour and appearance form part of the physical examination.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Urine culture is a separate microbiological test, not part of routine urinalysis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Volume is recorded in the physical examination, particularly for 24-hour collections.

questions.pearl: Routine urine R/E: physical (colour, volume, SG), chemical (protein, sugar, ketones) and microscopy (cells, casts, crystals).

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Trichomoniasis gives a frothy greenish-yellow discharge with itching and strawberry cervix.

options.label: B
options.explanation: BV gives a thin grey fishy-smelling discharge, typically without itching or inflammation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Candida causes intense pruritus with a thick curdy white discharge.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cervical cancer causes blood-stained or foul discharge and contact bleeding, not itching.

questions.pearl: Amsel criteria for BV: thin homogeneous discharge, pH over 4.5, positive whiff test, clue cells (3 of 4).

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chlamydia trachomatis (D-K) is the commonest bacterial STI and a major cause of PID.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Candida is mainly endogenous but can be sexually transmitted and is listed among sexually transmitted infections.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HSV-2 (and increasingly HSV-1) causes genital herpes spread sexually.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bacteroides are commensal anaerobes; they participate in mixed infections but are not sexually transmitted.

questions.pearl: Chlamydia L1-L3 serovars cause lymphogranuloma venereum.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dengue causes a maculopapular or confluent erythematous rash with islands of white in a sea of red.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Measles rash is maculopapular, starting behind the ears and spreading downward on day 4.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Secondary syphilis gives a generalised maculopapular rash involving palms and soles.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Herpes zoster gives a dermatomal vesicular rash, not maculopapular.

questions.pearl: Rash on palms and soles: secondary syphilis, hand-foot-mouth disease, rickettsiae, erythema multiforme, Kawasaki disease.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: They are highly lipid soluble and cross the blood-brain barrier, unlike second-generation drugs.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Most act for only 4-6 hours and need repeated dosing.

options.label: C
options.explanation: CNS H1 blockade causes marked sedation and psychomotor impairment.

options.label: D
options.explanation: They have additional anticholinergic and antiemetic actions, making them useful in motion sickness and pruritus.

questions.pearl: Promethazine and diphenhydramine sedate; cetirizine, loratadine and fexofenadine are minimally sedating.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Near term it can cause grey baby syndrome because the neonatal liver cannot conjugate it.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cephalosporins are considered safe in pregnancy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Tetracyclines stain fetal teeth, depress bone growth and can cause maternal fatty liver.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Erythromycin base is considered safe in pregnancy; only the estolate salt is avoided because of cholestatic hepatitis.

questions.pearl: Also avoid in pregnancy: aminoglycosides (ototoxicity), fluoroquinolones, cotrimoxazole near term (kernicterus).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rifampicin is a potent CYP3A4 inducer, reducing levels of OCPs, warfarin and antiretrovirals.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ketoconazole is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Carbamazepine induces hepatic enzymes, including its own metabolism (autoinduction).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Metronidazole inhibits warfarin metabolism and has a disulfiram-like effect.

questions.pearl: Inducers mnemonic GPRS Cell Phone: griseofulvin, phenytoin, rifampicin, smoking, carbamazepine, phenobarbitone.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Clinical features of acute suppurative otitis media:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Severe throbbing earache is typical in the stage of suppuration.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pus under pressure makes the tympanic membrane red and bulging with loss of landmarks.

options.label: C
options.explanation: ASOM causes conductive hearing loss from fluid in the middle ear.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fever, often high in children, accompanies the stage of suppuration.

questions.pearl: Once the drum perforates and discharge begins, the pain and fever usually settle.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Sterilisation methods that destroy bacterial spores:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dry heat at 160 C for 2 hours kills spores and is used for glassware and powders.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Moist heat at 121 C and 15 psi for 15 minutes kills spores; Geobacillus stearothermophilus is the control.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Incineration burns material to ash and destroys all microbes including spores; used for infected waste.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Gamma rays (cold sterilisation) kill spores and are used for disposable plastics.

questions.pearl: Autoclave biological indicator: Geobacillus stearothermophilus; ethylene oxide and dry heat: Bacillus atrophaeus.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Laryngomalacia is the commonest cause of congenital stridor, worse on feeding and supine.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Acute epiglottitis (H. influenzae b) causes rapidly progressive stridor with drooling.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Viral laryngotracheobronchitis causes inspiratory stridor and barking cough.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bronchiolitis affects small airways and causes wheeze and crackles, not stridor.

questions.pearl: Stridor arises from the larynx or trachea; wheeze arises from smaller airways.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Beta blockers, even cardioselective ones, can precipitate bronchospasm and are avoided in asthma.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Inhaled corticosteroids are the cornerstone of controller therapy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Salmeterol is a long-acting beta-2 agonist, always combined with an inhaled steroid.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Montelukast is a leukotriene receptor antagonist used as add-on therapy.

questions.pearl: LABA monotherapy in asthma increases asthma deaths; always pair it with an inhaled steroid.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Aedes aegypti, a daytime biter, is the main vector of dengue.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chikungunya is spread by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Aedes aegypti transmits urban yellow fever.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Malaria is transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.pearl: Aedes also spreads Zika; Culex spreads Japanese encephalitis and filariasis.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Causes of consolidation in the right lung:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Lobar pneumonia is the classic cause of consolidation with bronchial breathing.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Tuberculous pneumonia can present as consolidation, often in the upper lobe.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Aspirated material goes preferentially to the right lung because the right main bronchus is wider and more vertical.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bronchiectasis causes dilated bronchi with coarse crackles, not consolidation as its defining picture.

questions.pearl: Supine aspiration affects the posterior segment of the right upper lobe and apical segment of the right lower lobe.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Clinical features of severe dehydration in children (IMCI):

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sunken eyes are one of the IMCI signs used to classify severe dehydration.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Skin pinch going back slowly indicates some dehydration; severe dehydration needs very slowly (over 2 seconds).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dry mouth is not one of the IMCI classifying signs.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Not able to drink or drinking poorly is an IMCI sign of severe dehydration.

questions.pearl: IMCI severe dehydration: two of lethargic/unconscious, sunken eyes, not able to drink, skin pinch goes back very slowly.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Unmyelinated C fibres carry slow, dull, burning pain.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Thinly myelinated A-delta fibres carry fast, sharp, well-localised pain.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A-beta fibres carry touch and pressure; they modulate pain in the gate control theory but do not carry it.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pain and temperature ascend in the lateral spinothalamic tract after crossing in the cord.

questions.pearl: Fast pain uses glutamate; slow pain uses substance P.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Diseases transmitted by the faeco-oral route:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hepatitis A spreads through contaminated food and water.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hepatitis C is blood-borne.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Salmonella Typhi spreads via faecally contaminated food and water.

options.label: D
options.explanation: HIV spreads through sexual, blood and vertical routes.

questions.pearl: Faeco-oral: hepatitis A and E, typhoid, cholera, polio, rotavirus, amoebiasis, ascariasis.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: A white pupillary reflex is the commonest presentation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Squint from loss of central vision is the second commonest presentation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Bilateral fixed dilated pupils are not a feature; only the affected eye may lose its reflex.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tumour growth and iris neovascularisation can cause secondary glaucoma with buphthalmos.

questions.pearl: Retinoblastoma: RB1 gene on 13q14; bilateral cases are hereditary and at risk of osteosarcoma.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Polio destroys anterior horn cells, causing asymmetric flaccid paralysis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Guillain-Barre syndrome is now the commonest cause of AFP, with ascending symmetrical weakness.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Acute transverse myelitis causes flaccid paraplegia during spinal shock.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Stroke is an upper motor neurone lesion; it is not counted as AFP in surveillance.

questions.pearl: AFP surveillance: any child under 15 with acute flaccid paralysis; two stool samples 24 h apart within 14 days.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Increased hepatic lipoprotein synthesis in response to low oncotic pressure causes hyperlipidaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Diabetes causes dyslipidaemia with raised triglycerides and LDL and low HDL.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Thyroid hormone upregulates LDL receptors, so cholesterol falls in hyperthyroidism; hypothyroidism raises it.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Excess pituitary hormones (e.g. GH) do not typically cause hypercholesterolaemia.

questions.pearl: Secondary hypercholesterolaemia: hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis, diabetes, drugs (thiazides, steroids).

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: The following are NOT immovable joints:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Gomphosis (tooth in socket) is a fibrous immovable joint.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Synostosis is bony fusion, e.g. a closed suture, so it is immovable.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Primary cartilaginous joints (synchondroses) such as the epiphyseal plate are immovable.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The knee is a synovial (freely movable) hinge joint, so it is not immovable.

questions.pearl: Symphyses (secondary cartilaginous) are slightly movable and lie in the midline: pubic symphysis, intervertebral discs.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Valproate is first-line for acute mania and rapid cycling.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Amitriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant and may precipitate mania in bipolar disorder.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Lead is a toxic heavy metal with no therapeutic role; lithium is the classic mood stabiliser.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Olanzapine is approved for acute mania and bipolar maintenance.

questions.pearl: Lithium therapeutic range 0.6-1.0 mmol/L; toxicity causes coarse tremor, ataxia and confusion.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Coagulation current uses interrupted high-voltage pulses to seal vessels.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fulguration sparks across the air to char tissue superficially.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Continuous low-voltage current vaporises cells to cut tissue.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Diathermy is not a treatment for infection.

questions.pearl: Bipolar diathermy is safer for appendages (penis, digits) and patients with pacemakers.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Features of healing by secondary intention:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Burn wounds with tissue loss heal by granulation, contraction and epithelialisation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Contaminated or tissue-loss wounds are left open to heal by secondary intention.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Apposed edges describe primary intention healing.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Large granulation tissue and contraction by myofibroblasts make healing slow, with more scarring.

questions.pearl: Tertiary intention (delayed primary closure) is suturing a contaminated wound after 3-5 days.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Clinical features of deviated nasal septum:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Obstruction, usually unilateral, is the commonest symptom.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Contact of a septal spur with the lateral wall can cause headache (contact point headache).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mucosa over a spur is exposed to drying air currents, crusts and bleeds, so epistaxis is recognised.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Compensatory hypertrophy of the turbinate occurs on the concave side.

questions.pearl: Septoplasty is preferred to SMR in children and preserves septal support.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Eye muscles that elevate the eye:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Superior rectus elevates, most powerfully with the eye abducted.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Inferior oblique elevates, most powerfully with the eye adducted.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Inferior rectus is a depressor.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Superior oblique depresses, especially in adduction, and intorts the eye.

questions.pearl: LR6 SO4, rest 3: lateral rectus by abducens, superior oblique by trochlear, all others by oculomotor.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Intensely itchy grouped vesicles on extensors, linked with gluten-sensitive enteropathy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Psoriasis causes well-demarcated scaly plaques; vesicles are not typical, only pustules in pustular forms.

options.label: C
options.explanation: SJS causes mucosal erosions and blisters with epidermal detachment under 10% of body surface.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Scabies typically causes burrows and papules; vesicles occur but are not a defining bullous lesion.

questions.pearl: Dermatitis herpetiformis: IgA granular deposits at dermal papillae; responds to dapsone and a gluten-free diet.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Carditis (pancarditis) is a major Jones criterion and the only one causing permanent damage.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sydenham chorea is a major criterion, often appearing late.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Raised ESR or CRP is a minor criterion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fever is a minor criterion.

questions.pearl: Major Jones criteria (JONES): joints, carditis, nodules, erythema marginatum, Sydenham chorea.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Low ionised calcium increases neuronal excitability, causing carpopedal spasm.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hypercalcaemia reduces excitability and causes weakness, not tetany.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Low magnesium impairs PTH secretion and action, causing hypocalcaemia and tetany.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Phosphate binds calcium, lowering ionised calcium and causing tetany.

questions.pearl: Alkalosis causes tetany by increasing protein binding of calcium; check Trousseau and Chvostek signs.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Right upper quadrant pain is part of Charcot's triad.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Obstruction of the bile duct causes jaundice.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fever with rigors reflects bacterial infection of obstructed bile.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Mucocele is a gallbladder complication of cystic duct obstruction, not a feature of cholangitis.

questions.pearl: Reynolds pentad = Charcot's triad plus hypotension and confusion; needs urgent biliary drainage (ERCP).

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Thick inspissated secretions cause meconium ileus in neonates and distal intestinal obstruction syndrome later.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Inspissated meconium obstructs the terminal ileum.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hirschsprung's causes functional obstruction of the rectum and colon (large bowel).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Adhesions are the commonest cause of small bowel obstruction in adults.

questions.pearl: Commonest causes of SBO: adhesions, then hernias; in large bowel, carcinoma then volvulus.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Urticarial reactions to plasma proteins are among the commonest complications.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Transmission of HBV, HCV, HIV, syphilis and malaria is possible.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Air can enter during pressurised infusion or line changes.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Citrate in stored blood chelates calcium, causing hypocalcaemia in massive transfusion.

questions.pearl: Massive transfusion: hypocalcaemia, hyperkalaemia, hypothermia, dilutional coagulopathy and acidosis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Saturated steam under pressure is the most reliable sterilisation method.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Incineration destroys contaminated material and all microbes completely.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Steaming at 100 C on three successive days kills spores that germinate between heatings.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Inspissation at 80-85 C on three successive days sterilises egg- and serum-containing media.

questions.pearl: Tyndallisation is used for sugar- and gelatin-containing media; inspissation for Lowenstein-Jensen and Loeffler serum media.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Optic nerve compression and exposure keratopathy can reduce vision, an emergency sign.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Orbital cellulitis does not deepen the anterior chamber; it lies outside the globe.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ocular movements are restricted and painful.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Inflamed orbital contents push the globe forward, causing proptosis.

questions.pearl: Proptosis, painful restricted movement and reduced vision distinguish orbital from preseptal cellulitis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Labetalol is a first-line oral and IV agent in pregnancy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Methyldopa has the longest safety record in pregnancy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: ACE inhibitors cause fetal renal failure, oligohydramnios and skull defects; contraindicated.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Diuretics reduce plasma volume, already low in pre-eclampsia, and are avoided.

questions.pearl: Severe hypertension in pregnancy: IV labetalol, oral nifedipine or IV hydralazine.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Mumps causes sensorineural (often unilateral) deafness, not otitis media; otitis media is a classic measles complication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Meningitis is common and encephalitis is a recognised serious complication.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mumps pancreatitis causes epigastric pain with raised amylase.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Keratitis is not a recognised mumps complication; dacryoadenitis can occur.

questions.pearl: Orchitis is the commonest complication in post-pubertal males, rarely causing sterility.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The cornea provides about two-thirds (~43 D) of the eye's refractive power.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sclera is opaque and does not transmit light.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The lens provides about 17-20 D and adjusts focus by accommodation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The retina is the light-sensitive layer, not a refractive medium.

questions.pearl: Refractive media: cornea, aqueous humour, lens, vitreous humour; the cornea-air interface is the strongest.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cholesteatoma can erode the fallopian canal and cause facial nerve palsy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Spread through the posterior fossa dura or labyrinth causes cerebellar abscess.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Orbital cellulitis is a complication of sinusitis, especially ethmoid, not CSOM.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Blindness is not a recognised complication of CSOM.

questions.pearl: Gradenigo syndrome (petrositis): ear discharge, retro-orbital pain and VI nerve palsy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fetal hyperglycaemia causes osmotic polyuria, increasing amniotic fluid.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Renal anomalies reduce fetal urine and cause oligohydramnios.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The fetus cannot swallow amniotic fluid, so it accumulates.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Impaired swallowing and transudation from exposed meninges cause polyhydramnios.

questions.pearl: Polyhydramnios: AFI over 24-25 cm or single deepest pocket over 8 cm.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pus in crypts gives yellowish-white spots on the tonsils.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Diphtheria forms a greyish-white membrane that bleeds on removal and extends beyond the tonsil.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fusospirochaetal infection causes a greyish membrane over an ulcerated tonsil.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ludwig's angina is cellulitis of the submandibular space from dental infection, not a tonsillar patch.

questions.pearl: Membrane on tonsil also in infectious mononucleosis, candidiasis, agranulocytosis and leukaemia.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Paranasal sinuses opening in the middle meatus:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The maxillary ostium opens into the hiatus semilunaris of the middle meatus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Anterior ethmoid cells drain into the middle meatus.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Posterior ethmoid cells drain into the superior meatus, and the sphenoid into the sphenoethmoidal recess.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The frontal sinus drains via the frontonasal duct into the middle meatus.

questions.pearl: Middle meatus mnemonic FAME: frontal, anterior ethmoid, maxillary; the nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus.
